name: Lateral raise
summary: Light dumbbells by the sides, raise the arms out to shoulder height with soft elbows, lower slowly.
setup: Face the phone, light dumbbells by the sides, slight bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are level with the shoulders, pause, lower slowly.
brief: Stand with light dumbbells by the sides, a slight bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides until level with the shoulders, pause, then lower slowly.
why: Facing the phone the wrists rise to shoulder height each rep, the shoulders hiking up shows as the ear–shoulder gap closing, and going above shoulder height is caught too.

show.ask: arms straight out to the sides, level with your shoulders, nothing in your hands

regression: Lighter; one arm with the other hand on a support.
contraindications: Shoulder pain lifting to the side (impingement).

faults.label: Raising above the shoulders
faults.tip: Above level the trapezius takes over and the joint pinches.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Swinging the weights up
faults.tip: If you need a swing, the weight is too heavy.

faults.label: Raising above shoulder height
faults.tip: Higher than shoulder level swaps the side of the shoulder for the upper trapezius.

faults.label: Swinging the weights up
faults.tip: If you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. This is a small muscle.

guide.stop: A pinch at the top of the shoulder.

points.t: Rise to shoulder height, not above; soft elbows.
